implementation_notes: Go's specific failure mode is structural embedding combined with the absence of inheritance: a new field on a shared embedded struct appears to require nothing (which is right) but breaks every composite literal that names fields without keys, and every type switch and copy. The idiomatic guard is keyed composite literals and keeping shared state behind a pointer to a named struct rather than embedding values. Adding a case to a type switch across a package is the other scatter; centralising the dispatch behind a map keyed by the concrete type keeps it in one file.
idiom_name: adding a field to every struct that embeds the shared one
pitfalls: Unexported-keyed literals (`Order{id: 1}`) break silently when a field is added; use keyed literals everywhere.
A type switch in each consumer of a message type is the same scatter in every package that handles it.
`go vet`'s exhaustive check only helps for enums expressed as named constants; type switches are unchecked.
